pageCache.text:
OAK TREES FROM LITTLE ACORNS GROW
Being Headteacher at Oakfield Church of England Primary School is both an honour and a privilege. Oakfield is a great school, with a fantastic staff team, amazing children and wonderful families. We pride ourselves on delivering a broad education and developing important Christian values that will help guide our children through life.
We are a fully inclusive school and will go above and beyond to get it right for every child, recognising that different children need different things to be treated equitably. We also recognise the importance of having strong mental health and this is supported, first and foremost, through the positive relationships we build with one another. With a wonderful school site, and so much to explore on our doorstep, we are lucky to be able to use our local environment to hook the children into new learning in purposeful and engaging ways.
If you would like to visit the school, please use the ‘Contact Us’ tab to arrange this. If you are a member of the Community, please don’t forget that our ‘Family and Community Hub’ has lots on offer and the onsite Community Pantry is open every Monday, Wednesday and Friday afternoons 3.15pm – 4.30pm.
Vikki Reader Headteacher

ADMISSIONS
Admissions process for starting primary school in September 2027
Admissions Policy 2026-2027
Who can apply?
Only a parent can apply for a place at a school. A parent is any person who has parental responsibility for or is the legal guardian of the child, as set out in the Children Act 1989.
How to apply
You must complete a Local Authority application form online available here. Should you wish to use a paper application, please contact the school office who will be pleased to issue you with one. The round opens on 1st September 2026.
Offering places
The Governing Body will consider first all those applications received by the published deadline of midnight 15th January 2027. Notifications to parents offering a school place will be sent by the Local Authority on 16th April 2027.
Applications made after midnight on 15th January will be considered after all on-time applications have been fully processed unless exceptional circumstances merit consideration alongside on-time applications.
For the normal admission round, all on time preferences will be considered simultaneously and ranked in accordance with the admission criteria. If more than one school can offer a place, the parent’s highest stated available preference will be allocated.
Appeals
If you are unsuccessful in being offered a place for your child at Oakfield Church of England (Aided) Primary School you will be informed by the Local Authority in writing, will be given reasons for the refusal and informed of your right to an independent appeal against the decision.
For more information, please contact us.
In-Year Applications 2026-2027
Who can apply?
Only a parent can apply for a place at a school. A parent is any person who has parental responsibility for or is the legal guardian of the child, as set out in the Children Act 1989.
How to apply
The allocation of any places, which may become available during the year, will be made on the basis of the current Admissions Criteria. There are no deadline dates for in year applications. Applications must be made using the Local Authority Admission Form available from website: www.iow.gov.uk. Any parent with parental responsibility can apply for a place for their child at any time to any school. The Governing Body will decide whether a place can be offered at this school.
In-Year Fair Access placements by the local authority
The local authority must ensure that all pupils are placed in schools as quickly as possible. It may therefore sometimes be necessary for a pupil to be placed by the local authority, or a local placement panel acting on behalf of the authority, in a particular school even if there is a waiting list for admission. Such placements will be made in accordance with the provisions of the local authority’s In-Year Fair Access Protocol. The Protocol is based on legislation and government guidance.
For more information, please see the In-year admissions page on the Local Authority website.
If you require further information about applying for a place at Oakfield Church of England (Aided) Primary School, please contact The School.
Email: office@oakfieldcepri.iow.sch.uk
If you require a hard copy of any of the documents from this website, please do not hesitate to contact the school.

Safeguarding
Keeping Our Children Safe
Are you worried about a child? Click here
Safeguarding at Oakfield
At Oakfield, the safety, wellbeing and happiness of every child is our highest priority. We are committed to providing a safe, caring and inclusive environment where children feel valued, respected and able to learn, thrive and achieve their full potential.
Safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility. Every member of staff, governor, volunteer and visitor has a role to play in keeping children safe and promoting their welfare.
What is Safeguarding?
Safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children means:
Protecting children from abuse, neglect and maltreatment.
Our Commitment
We recognise that safeguarding extends beyond child protection and includes areas such as attendance, mental health and wellbeing, online safety, bullying, peer-on-peer abuse, child criminal exploitation, child sexual exploitation, domestic abuse, radicalisation and extremism.
Working Together
Our staff are often in a position to identify concerns early and provide support before issues escalate. We work in partnership with children’s social care, health services, the police and other agencies to safeguard and promote the welfare of children.
Our Safeguarding Team
Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL)
Miss Rebecca Howlett
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Leads (DDSLs)
Mrs Vikki Reader Mrs Hannah Doyle Mrs Cara Webster (Nursery)
Family Liason Officer and Children’s Champion
The safeguarding team is available to provide support, advice and guidance to children, families and staff.
If You Have a Concern
If you have any concerns about the safety or welfare of a child, please contact a member of our safeguarding team immediately.
If you believe a child is at immediate risk of harm, contact the police on 999.
Safeguarding information leaflet for visitors
Useful Contacts
Isle of Wight Multi-Agency Safeguarding Hub (MASH) 01983 823435
Local Authority Designated Officer (LADO) For concerns about adults working with children or those in positions of trust 01983 823723 lado@iow.gov.uk
Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary 101 (non-emergency) or 999 (emergency)
NSPCC Helpline 0808 800 5000
Stop It Now! Confidential Helpline 0808 1000 900 www.stopitnow.org.uk
Please refer below for key documents:
Keeping Children Safe in Education Sept 2025
Working Together to Safeguard Children (DfE)
Online Safety
Technology plays an important role in children’s lives, offering valuable opportunities for learning, creativity and communication. At Oakfield, we are committed to helping children develop the knowledge, skills and confidence they need to use technology safely, responsibly and respectfully.
Online safety is an integral part of our safeguarding curriculum and is taught through Computing, PSHE, assemblies and everyday classroom discussions. Children learn how to:
We recognise that the online world is constantly evolving, and we work closely with parents and carers to support children both in school and at home.
Protect their personal information and privacy online.
Recognise and respond to online risks.
Build positive and respectful relationships online.
Identify misinformation and unreliable content.
Support for Parents and Carers
We encourage parents and carers to take an active interest in their child’s online activity. Talking regularly about online experiences, setting clear boundaries and using parental controls can help children navigate the digital world safely.
If you have concerns about your child’s online safety, please speak to a member of our safeguarding team.
Useful Online Safety Resources
National Online Safety — https://nationalcollege.com/parents Free guides and resources for parents covering apps, games, social media and online trends.
Internet Matters – https://www.internetmatters.org/ Expert advice for parents on setting controls, managing screen time and keeping children safe online.
NSPCC Online Safety – https://www.nspcc.org.uk/keeping-children-safe/online-safety/ Practical advice on online gaming, social media, live streaming and talking to children about online risks.
Childnet – https://www.childnet.com/ Resources and guidance to help children and families stay safe online.
Thinkuknow – https://saferinternet.org.uk/resource/thinkuknow-advice-from-ceop Education resources from the National Crime Agency’s CEOP Education Team.
UK Safer Internet Centre – https://saferinternet.org.uk/ Advice, resources and reporting tools for parents, carers and young people.
Reporting Concerns
If your child has experienced online abuse, exploitation or inappropriate contact, concerns can be reported directly to CEOP (Child Exploitation and Online Protection Command).
Remember: if a child is in immediate danger, contact the police on 999.
Safeguarding Documents
Please see our Policies page for key safeguarding documents, including:
We are committed to working in partnership with families to ensure every child is safe, supported and able to flourish.
Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE) 2025
Working Together to Safeguard Children
Isle of Wight Safeguarding Children Partnership guidance
Safer Recruitment and the Single Central Record
Oakfield is committed to ensuring that all adults working with children are suitable to do so and that robust safeguarding procedures are in place.
As required by the Department for Education, the school maintains a Single Central Record (SCR). This confidential record contains details of all required pre-employment and safeguarding checks for staff, governors, volunteers and other adults working within the school.
These checks include:
The Single Central Record is regularly monitored and reviewed to ensure compliance with statutory safeguarding requirements and safer recruitment guidance.
Identity verification
Right to work in the UK
Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) checks
Children’s Barred List checks (where applicable)
Qualifications and professional status checks
Prohibition from teaching checks (where applicable)
Safeguarding and child protection training records
Allegations Against Staff and Volunteers
Oakfield takes all concerns and allegations relating to adults working with children seriously and will respond promptly, fairly and in accordance with statutory guidance.
Any concern that an adult working in the school may have:
will be managed in line with our safeguarding procedures and the guidance set out in Keeping Children Safe in Education.
Concerns about a member of staff should be reported to the Headteacher.
Concerns or allegations regarding the Headteacher should be reported to the Chair of Governors.
Where appropriate, the school will seek advice from the Local Authority Designated Officer (LADO).
LADO Contact Details 01983 823723 lado@iow.gov.uk
Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) Checks
The Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) helps schools make safer recruitment decisions and prevent unsuitable individuals from working with children.
Oakfield carries out all legally required DBS and safeguarding checks before adults begin working with pupils. However, safeguarding is not reliant on DBS checks alone. We follow a comprehensive safer recruitment process, including references, employment history checks, identity verification and safeguarding interviews.
Overseas Checks
Where an applicant has lived or worked overseas, the school will carry out additional checks in accordance with current Department for Education guidance. This may include obtaining a Certificate of Good Conduct or equivalent documentation from the relevant country.
These checks form part of our commitment to ensuring that every adult working within our school is suitable to work with children.
Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE)
At Oakfield, Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE) forms an important part of our curriculum and contributes to our wider safeguarding and wellbeing provision.
Our RSHE curriculum (SCARF) helps children to:
RSHE is delivered in an age-appropriate way and reflects statutory guidance from the Department for Education.
We believe that effective RSHE supports children to develop the knowledge, skills and understanding they need to thrive in modern Britain and to make informed, responsible choices as they grow.
For further information, please see our RSHE Policy available on the Policies page.
Build positive, healthy and respectful relationships.
Recognise appropriate and inappropriate behaviour.
Develop confidence, resilience and self-respect.
Statutory Guidance for Schools (updated September 2026)
Children Looked After (Children in Care)
At Oakfield, we are committed to supporting the educational achievement, wellbeing and personal development of children who are looked after by a local authority.
We recognise that children in care may have experienced significant challenges and that they often require additional support to help them achieve their full potential.
The school works closely with:
to ensure that each child receives the support, stability and opportunities they need to succeed.
We are committed to promoting high aspirations, positive relationships and a sense of belonging for all children in our care.
Further information about support available for children looked after can be found through the Isle of Wight Virtual School.
Foster carers and residential care providers
Social workers
The Virtual School
Other professionals involved in a child’s care
Supporting Pupils with Medical Conditions
At Oakfield, we are committed to ensuring that children with medical conditions are fully supported so that they can access education safely and successfully. We believe that all pupils should have the same opportunities to participate in school life, including learning, educational visits, physical activity and extracurricular activities, wherever it is safe and appropriate to do so.
We recognise that medical conditions can affect children in different ways. Some children may require short-term support following illness or injury, whilst others may have long-term or complex medical needs that require ongoing planning and care.
We work closely with parents, carers, healthcare professionals and external agencies to ensure that appropriate arrangements are in place to support each child’s individual needs. Effective communication and partnership working are central to ensuring that children remain safe, included and able to achieve their full potential.
Where required, Individual Healthcare Plans (IHPs) are developed in collaboration with families and relevant healthcare professionals. These plans help staff understand a child’s condition, the support they may need and the action to take in an emergency.
Our staff receive appropriate training and guidance to support pupils with medical conditions and to ensure that they can respond effectively to individual healthcare needs.
Working in Partnership
Parents and carers play a vital role in supporting their child’s medical needs and are responsible for informing the school of any medical conditions, changes to treatment, medication requirements or healthcare advice that may affect their child’s time in school.
We work collaboratively with a range of professionals and services, including:
School Nursing Services
General Practitioners (GPs)
Paediatricians and Specialist Consultants
Occupational Therapists
Community Healthcare Teams
Local Authority Services
Future Developments
The Government has announced proposed changes to legislation relating to support for children with medical conditions in schools, often referred to as Benedict’s Law. We are in the process of reviewing and updating our policies, procedures and website information as further statutory guidance becomes available, ensuring that our practice continues to meet legal requirements and reflects best practice.
Further Information
Our arrangements for supporting pupils with medical conditions are guided by the Department for Education’s statutory guidance:
Supporting Pupils at School with Medical Conditions
https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/5ce6a72e40f0b620a103bd53/supporting-pupils-at-school-with-medical-conditions.pdf
Please see our Policies page for our full Supporting Pupils with Medical Conditions Policy and related procedures.
Domestic Abuse Support
At Oakfield, we recognise that domestic abuse can have a significant impact on children and young people, whether they witness it directly, hear it, or experience its effects within the home. We are committed to supporting children and families and helping them access appropriate support when it is needed.
Domestic abuse can affect anyone, regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexuality or background. It may include physical, emotional, psychological, sexual, financial or controlling and coercive behaviour.
If you are concerned about your own safety, the safety of a child, or someone you know, support is available.
In an Emergency
If you or someone else is in immediate danger, always call 999.
The Silent Solution
If you are unable to speak when calling 999 from a mobile phone:
This alerts the operator that you are experiencing a genuine emergency and allows your call to be transferred to the police.
Dial 999.

When prompted, press 55.

Parent Community Group
The Parent Community Group (PCG) is an organisation of parents/carers, members of the community and staff. It is a strategic group and its role is to encourage closer links between home, school and the community. The PCG co-ordinate a calendar of events throughout the year; some will be fundraising for the school, others will be to promote community cohesion and ultimately enhance the opportunities available for children and their families within the community. They meet regularly at school. Past events have included Break the rules day’ for Children in Need, a Glow Party, Tea with Santa and the Grinch and OakFest!
If you would like more information about how to get involved please email pcg@oakfieldcepri.iow.sch.uk

SCHOOL MEALS
The food children eat in school is very important for their education. Not only does a well-balanced diet help with general health but establishing healthy eating habits at a young age can give them knowledge for the future.
Our catering company understand primary school children and their likes and dislikes so work with us to tailor our menus to encourage maximum uptake.
At Oakfield children are able to choose from a main meal or vegetarian option each day. If they prefer they may order a filled baguette, wrap or jacket potato. The menu choices rotate over a period of three weeks, so children have the opportunity to try lots of interesting and varied meals.
If you think you are entitled to food vouchers or have any questions about school meals, please get in touch with Mrs Taylor via contactus@oakfieldcepri.iow.sch.uk

pageCache.text:
Our Curriculum
At Oakfield CE Aided Primary school we have worked hard collectively to ensure that our curriculum intent is more than an ambition or something created in response to a latest buzz word, but is something that is underpinned by the national curriculum. The progression of skills and knowledge within our planning reflect what our children need in the medium and longer term. How we implement our curriculum offer reflects the fabric of who we are and we are and we pride ourselves in being able to clearly articulate why we are doing what we are doing. We have asked ourselves the long overdue question, is it time to rethink the way in which we educate our children so that they can be better prepared for the world we currently live in?
Through our schools values, Love, Trust, Honesty, Hope and our vision statement, ‘Belong, Believe, Achieve’, we are unwavering in our commitment to provide an education that is relevant, reflects the needs of our children and community and is enhanced by high quality resources and facilities. We are passionate about school improvement, self-reflection and self-improvement (not change for change sake). We remain consistent to our vision and principles.

pageCache.text:
GOVERNORS
The Governing Board plays an important role in supporting Oakfield CE Primary School and helping to ensure that every child receives the best possible education.
We work closely with the Headteacher and staff to help shape the school’s future, monitor its progress and make sure resources are used effectively. Our role is to provide support, ask questions, and help ensure that decisions are always made in the best interests of our children.
Everything we do is guided by Oakfield’s vision of “Belong, Believe, Achieve” and our Christian values of Love, Trust, Honesty and Hope. We want every child to feel safe, valued and included, to enjoy learning, and to leave Oakfield with the confidence and skills they need for the next stage of their education.
Our governors come from a range of backgrounds and bring different skills and experiences to the board. We all share a commitment to supporting the school, its staff, its families and, most importantly, its children.
We are proud to be part of the Oakfield family and to serve a school community where children are encouraged to grow, thrive and achieve their full potential.
If you would like to contact the Governing Board, please do so through the school office.
